overview: SARS collects taxes that fund government services. Every person who earns income above certain thresholds must register as a taxpayer and submit annual tax returns. SARS also handles VAT registration, customs, and tax clearance certificates.

who_must_register: Any person earning above R95,750 per year from a single employer
Anyone earning income from more than one source
Anyone with a provisional tax obligation
Anyone earning rental income, freelance income, or investment income
how_to_register: Visit www.sarsefiling.co.za and create an eFiling account
Or visit your nearest SARS branch with your ID and proof of address
You will receive a tax reference number — KEEP THIS SAFE, you will need it forever

filing_your_tax_return.when: Tax season runs from July to November each year (dates announced by SARS annually)
how: Your employer's IRP5 certificate should be pre-populated
Check that the amounts match your payslips
Add any additional income (freelance, rental, investments)
Claim allowable deductions (medical aid contributions, retirement fund contributions, travel allowance)
SARS will issue an assessment — either you owe SARS or SARS owes you a refund
first_time_tips: Keep all your payslips — they are your proof if SARS questions anything
Your IRP5 certificate comes from your employer — ask HR for it
If you earned below the threshold and had tax deducted, you MAY get a refund
Medical aid tax credits are automatic if your employer reported them correctly
You can claim for home office expenses ONLY if you have a dedicated room used exclusively for work

common_problems: Employer did not submit IRP5 — contact your employer immediately, then report to SARS if they refuse
Assessment shows you owe money you don't have — apply for a payment arrangement at SARS
Received assessment for tax you don't owe — dispute the assessment within 30 days on eFiling
eFiling not working — clear your browser cache, try a different browser, or visit a SARS branch
Outstanding tax returns from previous years — file them all, starting with the oldest year

tax_clearance_certificate.what_it_is: A document confirming that your tax affairs are in order. Required for government tenders, certain visa applications, and large financial transactions.
how_to_get: Apply on SARS eFiling under 'Tax Compliance Status'
Your tax returns must be up to date and any debt must be settled or under a payment arrangement
Processing is usually immediate if your affairs are in order
If there are issues, SARS will tell you what needs to be resolved first

vat_registration.who_must_register: Any business with taxable supplies exceeding R1 million per year
vat_registration.voluntary_registration: Businesses with taxable supplies exceeding R50,000 per year may register voluntarily
how_to_register: Provide proof of business activity, bank statements, invoices
SARS may conduct a verification visit
Once registered, you must submit VAT returns every 2 months

sars_offices_ethekwini.name: SARS Durban CBD
sars_offices_ethekwini.address: Kingsmead Office Park, 2 Kingsmead Way, Durban
sars_offices_ethekwini.tip: Book an appointment online before visiting — walk-ins face very long waits

escalation.step_1: Use SARS eFiling to dispute an assessment — you have 30 business days from the assessment date
escalation.step_2: If SARS does not resolve your dispute, request Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) through eFiling
escalation.step_3: If ADR fails, appeal to the Tax Court
escalation.step_4: Contact the Tax Ombud for complaints about SARS service: 0800 662 837
escalation.legislation: Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, Income Tax Act 58 of 1962

your_rights: You have the right to be treated fairly and with respect at any SARS office
You have the right to clear explanations of any tax assessment
You have the right to dispute any assessment within 30 business days
You have the right to a payment arrangement if you cannot pay your tax debt in full
SARS must process refunds within a reasonable time — persistent delays can be reported to the Tax Ombud
You have the right to confidentiality of your tax information
SARS may not attach your primary residence to settle tax debt below R250,000 without a court order
